title: gpu-firmware-interrupt-workaround-and-oncall-cheatsheet
content:
Purpose:
Quick working notes for oncall when a subset of dedicated GPU hosts show transient compute stalls believed to be caused by firmware interrupts / noisy-tenant KV-cache amplification. This is a compact, pragmatic cheat-sheet: timeline template, detection signals, immediate mitigations, triage commands, and medium-term actions to avoid repeating runway degradations.

Context and why this differs from other notes:
- Recent incidents show a class of partial degradation where pods keep running but effective token throughput and P95 latency degrade in bursts for a subset of hosts.
- Symptoms don't always look like normal CPU/GPU saturation — often driver/firmware interrupt storms or pathological host-level PCIe errors.
- Traditional autoscaler and eviction policies sometimes make things worse (cascade eviction, slow recovery). This doc focuses on quick detection and a low-risk rollback path.

Incident template (fill during oncall):
- Incident ID: INFRA-2458 (example)
- First alert: T0 (UTC) - name of alert/dash: gpu-host-interrupt-rate-high / p95-latency-dedicated-pool
- Observed impact: spike in per-host interrupt rate, per-GPU compute stalls, high queue depth in request-router
- Scope: affected pools, customer tenants (tenant IDs), percentage of GPUs impacted
- Initial oncall action (T0 -> T+15m): isolate noisy hosts from allocator, move heavy tenants to burst-reserve, reduce per-tenant concurrency by 30%

Detection signals (dashboards / logs):
- dashboards/dedicated/pool-health -> p95 latency by pool and host heatmap
- metrics: gpu_interrupts{host}, gpu_utilization_free (drop), nvml-process-errors, host_pci_errors
- request_router metrics: queue_depth_by_pool, in_flight_per_tenant
- logs: dmesg/syslog on host: repeated PCIe-reset or NVML WARN messages
- traces: tail-sampled traces showing long polling waits for cache/KV hits

Immediate mitigations (0-30 minutes):
1) Soft isolate: mark host as drainage-candidate in pool manager (do not evict immediately).
   - Command: curl -X POST $POOL_MGR/api/host/mark?host=host-xyz&state=drain-candidate
   - Rationale: flagging gives autoscaler signals without thrashing eviction loops.
2) Rapid tenant fencing: move top-2 noisy tenants off affected host group to burst pool.
   - Command: route manager: POST /route/reassign {tenant: T123, pool: burst-pool}
3) Throttle per-tenant concurrency remotely: reduce concurrency setting via feature-flag (config service)
   - Quick rollback knob: set config key dedicated.concurrency.scale = 0.7
4) If NV driver shows persistent PCIe errors -> escalate hardware team and trigger host reboot on scheduled window; prefer live-evacuation only if queue depth < 10 and clients can tolerate failover.

Commands and checks for triage (safe copy-paste):
- kubectl get pods -n dedicated --selector=pool=dedicated-pool -o wide
- curl $METRICS_HOST/metrics?query=gpu_interrupts{pool="dedicated-pool"}
- ssh host-xyz "sudo journalctl -u nvidia-driver -n 200 | tail -n 100"
- ssh host-xyz "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu --format=csv,noheader,nounits"
- curl $POOL_MGR/api/pool/status?pool=dedicated-pool | jq .host_status
- dispatch: /usr/local/bin/reassign-tenant --tenant T123 --target burst-pool (internal helper)

Hypotheses to validate (ranked):
- H1 (most likely): KV cache amplification from specific tenant prompts high PCIe traffic -> interrupt storms -> compute stalls.
- H2: Driver/firmware regression on a small host subset causing poor interrupt coalescing.
- H3: Autoscaler misconfiguration (eviction thresholds too aggressive) leading to cascading moves and transient overloads on remaining hosts.

Notes on autoscaler misconfig interaction (why common mitigation backfires):
- Autoscaler sees rising p95 and attempts to evict pods to meet latency SLO. Evicted work migrates and increases load on healthy hosts -> triggers further eviction.
- Proposed immediate change during incident: set autoscaler.eviction.rate_limit=LOW and disable warm-fallback routing for 10-30 minutes.

Longer-term mitigations and action items (post-incident):
- A1: Implement per-host firmware health metric export (interrupt-rate) + alert when > X for 5m.
- A2: Add a graded eviction policy: prefer 'tenant-cooperative-eviction' (ask client to retry) before hard host eviction.
- A3: Build an automated noisy-tenant quarantine: shard by tenant heatmap and automatically move top N noisy tenants to isolated burst-pool when host-level interrupts exceed threshold.
- A4: Add a rollout gate in the GPU operator that blocks driver/firmware upgrades if host interrupt-rate baseline jumps > 2x historical.
- A5: Update runbook UI with quick toggles: drain-candidate marker, autoscaler-rate-limit, burst-pool-reassign with one-click in Console.

Post-incident rollback plan (safe steps):
- If mitigation causes client regressions, reverse in this order: 1) restore autoscaler.eviction.rate_limit to previous value, 2) re-enable warm-fallback routing, 3) reassign tenants back from burst-pool gradually with canary reassign.

Escalation criteria and hipri touchpoints:
- If >30% of a pool's GPUs show interrupts above threshold for 20m -> page hardware-oncall and SRE lead.
- If customers impacted > 5% of requests or an enterprise SLA breach is imminent -> page PS and account managers (Priya Shah).

Playbook improvements to implement this quarter (w/ owners):
- Miguel: implement telemetry export for gpu_interrupts metric (INFRA-2469)
- Liam: console toggle for drain-candidate + one-click reassign (UI-118)
- Anya: write quarantine automation spec and test harness (RFC due in 2 weeks)

Open questions / TODOs for follow-up during postmortem:
- How aggressive should automatic quarantine be without false positives? (tune window, multiplier)
- Can we get vendor visibility into per-host interrupt coalescing tuning options?
- Is there a hardware-level workaround (BIOS/firmware knob) safe for production?

Appendix: quick reference timings and simple SLO checks:
- SLO quick checks: p95 latency by pool, >10% increase sustained 5m -> incident mode; queue_depth > 50 sustained -> consider soft-drain
- Quick thresholds (starter): gpu_interrupts > 500/min per-host for 5m, queue_depth_by_pool > 30, eviction_rate > 0.2 evictions/min

Last oncall notes (hand-off):
- T+00:00 alert fired: p95 spike in dedicated-pool; observed host-abc interrupts 750/min
- T+00:08: soft isolate host-abc -> mark drain-candidate; moved tenant T867 and T341 to burst (manual)
- T+00:22: reduced concurrency flag to 0.7, observed p95 improve 18%
- T+00:45: host reboot scheduled for 01:00 UTC by infra-hardware; hardware team to follow up
- Owner for follow-up: Anya Patel (eng-sre), postmortem PR: INFRA-2458/postmortem-draft

Voice-of-oncall notes: messy, but the reduce-concurrency + soft-isolate combo appears low-risk and effective. Avoid immediate hard-eviction unless queue depth is tiny.

End of cheat-sheet. Keep this doc short and iterative — will convert to formal runbook after two successful fire drills.
